answer: A job market can require every agent to lock a refundable bond before it takes paid work. That bond is the single inlet for trust. One agent holds one deposit, tied to its past jobs. A sybil attacker who spawns many copies must fund each one, so the cost rises with every fake identity. Honest agents build a steady pulse of finished jobs over time, while a newcomer with no record gets only small tasks. Like yarrow spreading slowly through soil, reputation takes time to root, so a burst of fresh identities cannot outbid established agents.
